summary.headline: Century Plyboards posted record Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 1,492 crores (+24.5% YoY) with consolidated EBITDA margin ex-forex at 13.6%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered record quarterly revenue of INR 1,492 crores, up 10.5% QoQ and 24.5% YoY, with consolidated EBITDA margin excluding forex losses at 13.6% versus 12.6% in Q3 and 12.1% a year ago. For FY26, revenue grew 19.2% and EBITDA ex-forex rose to INR 702 crores (13.0% margin) from INR 502 crores (11.1%), with PAT up 44% to INR 268 crores. Management has taken a 7% plywood price increase in April and an industry-wide 15% increase in MDF/particle board amid chemical and resin cost inflation, but gave no FY27 segment guidance, citing fluid geopolitical conditions. Capex is focused on plywood (Hoshiarpur, UP, Orissa land), with no frozen capex for MDF or particle board.

financial_highlights.value: Growth 11.4% QoQ, 17.9% YoY; EBITDA margin ex-forex 16.1%

financial_highlights.change: Revenue +8.9% QoQ, +31% YoY; margin down ~1 pt QoQ

segments.name: Plywood
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +11.4% QoQ and +17.9% YoY with 16.1% EBITDA margin ex-forex; FY26 revenue +15.6%, EBITDA margin 15.2%. Capacity utilisation near 99% in Q4 per Nikita Bansal; current capacity 4,06,000 CBM as of March 2026.

segments.name: Laminates
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +8.3% QoQ and +16.3% YoY, EBITDA margin 10.3%; FY26 revenue +13.9% with margin 8.5% vs 5.2% in FY25. Badvel thick-laminate plant utilisation 47%; overall utilisation 84% on 87.7 lakh sheets capacity.

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +8.9% QoQ and +31% YoY, EBITDA margin ex-forex 11.3% after ~1 pt QoQ erosion from chemical-related disruptions and one-off ATL spend; FY26 revenue +25.5%, margin 12.7% vs 10.1%. Utilisation ~80-85%; Badvel shut down in Q4 to add 20% capacity; South plant brownfield adds 60,000-70,000 CBM in Q1 FY27 (total to ~6 lakh CBM).

segments.name: Particle Board
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +3.9% QoQ and +108.3% YoY, EBITDA margin 7.2%; FY26 revenue +38.2% but FY26 EBITDA margin only 1.2%. Old multi-daylight plant shut and to be scrapped; new continuous line capacity 2,40,000 CBM, Chennai plant cost cited at ~INR 550 crores.

segments.name: Century Ports
segments.commentary: Wholly owned subsidiary commenced commercial operations at KPD-1 West, Kolkata, in Q4 FY26; management expects it to be cash positive from Q1 FY27. Management said no cost saving accrues to Century Ply; it remains a separate profit centre.

guidance_outlook: No segment-wise FY27 guidance given; management said the situation is too fluid, with a stated intent to provide guidance at the next call.
Management expects ROE and ROCE to improve further as it sweats assets built over the last 3 years.
MDF steady-state EBITDA margin targeted in the high teens, timeline not specified.
Plywood planning assumes muted 10-12% volume growth and 80% utilisation for expansion planning.
Long-term debt not expected to exceed 1:1 debt-to-EBITDA; working capital debt expected to rise with growth.
Laminates expected to outgrow the industry by 3-4 percentage points.
capex_capacity: Plywood: Hoshiarpur plant (48,000 CBM) due in October 2026 (second half FY27); brownfield expansion at Kandla, Chennai and Guwahati adds ~20% (Chennai ~25,000-30,000 CBM by July 2026).

Plywood: UP plant capex expected to start late FY27 (Feb-March 2027 or Q1 FY28), commissioning in about 15-16 months after land is ready, targeted around Q1 FY29; Orissa land procurement underway (MoU covers plywood or MDF/particle board, nothing finalised).
MDF: South plant brownfield expansion adds 60,000-70,000 CBM per year, completion targeted by end of Q1 FY27; no further MDF capacity firmed up.
Particle board: new 2,40,000 CBM continuous line running; old plant to be scrapped with no plan to revive.

Capex for FY27-28 is predominantly plywood-directed; no frozen capex for MDF or particle board. Management cited ~INR 2,000 crores of total capex over the next 4-5 years as an analyst estimate, not confirmed by management.
Century Ports absorbed roughly INR 260-270 crores of spend over three years, per analyst.
demand_pricing: Plywood: 7% price increase taken in April 2026, with further hikes contingent on the chemical and timber trend; management described it as wait-and-watch.
MDF and particle board: industry-wide price increase of about 15% in Q4 FY26, which management said barely covers the chemical-driven cost rise; some peers have made selective rollbacks.
Vishu Goel said MDF and plywood price increases of 10-12% were largely in Q1 and predominantly cover chemical cost increases.
Timber prices reported as broadly stable; management described a marginal correction, not 10%.
Plywood secondary demand stable post price increase, per management; MDF demand described as stable with normal April-May correction from Q4 exuberance.
March 2026 channel stocking was cited as a partial driver of MDF Q4 volume growth; management said April was not slow.
Plywood Sainik MR (around 8% of revenue last quarter) is being moved in-house after Hoshiarpur comes online, to reach 100% in-house production.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of MDF's ~39% YoY growth, utilisation and price increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Sumant Wattas cited year-end stocking, network expansion in the South and secondary-channel demand; utilisation 80-85% of rated capacity, with a practical max of 85-90%. Industry price increase of 15% barely covers chemical cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company give FY27 segment guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal said the situation is too fluid to guide now; management expects to be in a better position at the next call.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity plans for plywood FY27-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Nikita Bansal said utilisation is near 99% in Q4 and capacity rises ~30% in FY27 (about 20% brownfield plus Hoshiarpur in October); a new plant is needed in FY28-29, with UP and Orissa land being procured.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the new particle board plant cost lower than earlier?
qa_highlights.answer: Sumant Wattas said the old multi-daylight plant (~INR 70 crores) was archaic and is being scrapped. The new continuous line cost about INR 550 crores, not INR 700 crores as the analyst cited.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook for MDF after Q4 erosion?
qa_highlights.answer: Sumant Wattas said Q4 margin fell ~1 pt QoQ from chemical disruptions and one-off ATL spend; steady state is a high-teens EBITDA margin, with no firm timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Debt levels, forex exposure and capex funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Arun Julasaria said long-term debt will not exceed 1:1 debt-to-EBITDA, working capital debt will rise with growth, and forex exposure is within INR 600 crores, mostly mark-to-market on long-term debt for imported machinery. Management is not increasing forex exposure.

risks_watch: Chemical (phenol, melamine, resin) and imported timber cost inflation tied to geopolitical disruption; management said the 15% price hike barely covers costs and its stickiness is unknown.
Possible price rollbacks by peers in MDF and particle board, which could affect pass-through and margins from Q1 FY27.
MDF margin recovery to high-teens EBITDA depends on chemical stabilisation; no timeline given.
Forex mark-to-market losses on long-term import debt, capped at about INR 600 crores by management.
Execution risk on Hoshiarpur (October 2026), South MDF brownfield (Q1 FY27), and UP and Orissa land timing.
Particle board FY26 EBITDA margin of only 1.2%; ramp-up of the new line is needed.
Plywood Sainik MR in-sourcing could constrain volume growth relative to the capacity addition.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 results and capacity growth, but deliberately cautious on forward numbers: management declined FY27 segment guidance, price-pass-through detail and chemical cost percentages, citing fluid geopolitics. Answers were sometimes inconsistent on capex and capacity figures, which the analyst challenged.
key_quotes: I'm pleased to share that the company reported its highest ever quarterly revenue of INR 1,492 crores during Q4 FY '26.
Excluding forex losses, ROE improved from 10.6% to 15.2%, while ROCE increased from 12.5% to 14.6%, reflecting stronger operational performance and improved capital efficiency.
So currently, there's no frozen capex for MDF or Particle Board, which are large substantial capexes.
But long-term debt, I don't think we'll exceed 1:1 EBITDA going forward.

Sanjay Agarwal: Actually, the present situation is so, I think, fluid, it will not be right on our part to give you anything right now, but maybe by next time, we will be in a better position to -- till now whatever we have projected, we have been able to mostly achieve.
